rationale: The request presents workflow-level obstruction across dashboard submission, email approval, retry recovery, and ownership, so Fructal applies and the no-modification request selects Redesign. The response defines a coherent replacement workflow with durable identity, idempotent retry, a dashboard source of truth, explicit lifecycle and ownership, email-mediated approval, escalation, nearby recovery, retained input, auditability, accessibility, and a proportionate verification plan. Execution evidence and unchanged fixture hashes confirm read-only inspection with no write attempt. It correctly separates the observed blocked fixture state from requester-reported duplicate and ownership claims, frames the design as unvalidated, and identifies material open decisions. No mode label was required because the user did not use an explicit mode phrase. The closing statement and link announcing application of Fructal Cap Design are unnecessary ceremony, though they do not invalidate the deliverable.
